KnightLoader 2.9.9 follows YouTube channels, playlists and Mediathek shows, never downloads the same video twice, and gets arte.tv videos again.

## ✨ Added

- **Subscribe to a YouTube channel, @handle or playlist by pasting its link.** KnightLoader finds the channel's feed and names the subscription after it, even while YouTube is slow to hand out the feed. A channel subscription can also bring the older videos: all of them, the last few, or those of the last few days. When a link holds nothing to subscribe to, KnightLoader says so in plain words. Thanks to @Revan335 for asking in [#330](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/330) and [#331](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/331).
- **Subscribe to a Mediathek show.** Paste a MediathekViewWeb search and pick "Subscribe to this search". New episodes arrive in the quality you choose, with subtitles if you like, named after the programme instead of the server's file name.
- **Each subscription decides how it downloads.** It picks video or audio only, a quality cap and which rows a video gets, and "Starts on its own" lets that one subscription skip the link collector.
- **Subscriptions can leave entries out by an exclude pattern or by length.** An entry whose title matches the pattern, or that is shorter or longer than you set, is skipped. The length comes from the feed or from a quick look at the video.
- **Downloads can be named after the channel or show and filed as a series.** Jellyfin and Plex get a show folder with tvshow.nfo, poster and fanart, a season per year and an episode NFO beside every file.
- **SponsorBlock for YouTube videos.** Sponsor reads, intros, reminders to subscribe and the other categories can be cut out or kept as chapters, for every video or per subscription.
- **A video you downloaded before is not downloaded twice.** KnightLoader remembers each video by its site and id. The same video under another link, playlist or subscription waits in the rejected links with the date and folder of the first download, and "Download anyway" fetches it again. Subscriptions check this on their own, and pasted links follow "Reject links already downloaded". Thanks to @Revan335 for [#333](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/333).
- **The Android app manages subscriptions.** You can list, add from a pasted link, edit, test and remove them on the phone.

## 🎨 Design

- **The Feed subscriptions card is called Subscriptions,** since it holds channels and Mediathek searches as well.

## ⚡ Improved

- **A video blocked in your country says so.** Geo blocks from yt-dlp, the Mediathek servers and ORF's stand-in clip end with a note on what helps, instead of a bare 403 or a ten-second placeholder that looks like a success.
- **The same hoster file counts as a duplicate under another address.** Short domains such as rg.to, tracking parameters and other link forms of 14 hosters are recognised as the file you already have.
- **Subscriptions remember what they added in a table of their own.** Hundreds of them fit, and a channel can remember up to 20,000 videos.
- **The phone and the other instances in your group see subscription addresses without their secrets.** Passkeys, API keys, tokens and sign-ins show as …, and saving a subscription there keeps the real address. The web interface still shows the whole address.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **arte.tv videos download again.** Every arte download gave up after ten retries with "Conflicting range" and left an empty file. KnightLoader asked yt-dlp to fetch everything in 10 MiB pieces, and arte serves its videos as slices of one large file, which those pieces break. KnightLoader now leaves the piece size to yt-dlp, which still splits YouTube downloads so YouTube does not slow them down.
- **Saving the settings keeps every subscription on its schedule.** Each save started every subscription's wait over, so an instance whose settings were saved more often than the interval never checked its feeds. A save now leaves the remaining wait alone. Only a changed interval moves it, and a shorter one applies at once. Thanks to @Revan335 for the requests in [#330](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/330) and [#331](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/331) that led to this fix.
- **Segment buttons in the app show their whole label.** Labels that only just fit, such as "2160p", ended in an ellipsis, and segments meant to take their label's width came out equal.
- **A subscription that remembers one entry says "1 entry".**

## 🌐 Translations

- **Every new text in the web interface and the app speaks all 42 languages.** The app takes the web's words, so both say the same thing.
